target_customer: Software engineering and security teams that need to protect sensitive data and track open source dependency vulnerabilities
problem: Teams struggled to encrypt sensitive data safely and later to cut through noisy vulnerability scanner alerts. LunaSec offered open source data security tooling and then LunaTrace, a hosted dependency scanner.
business_model: Open source core with hosted paid product (LunaTrace); pricing not found
product_category: Open source application and dependency security

founders.name: Free Wortley
founders.background_notes: YC page describes a security engineer background in AI security and AppSec; no employers named.

founders.name: Matthew Bryant
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page with no background.

exit.reason: The YC page says LunaSec is dead and asks people to email the founder; no reason is given.

technical_complexity.rationale: Per-record encryption and tokenization needed careful cryptographic engineering, and the later scanner needed vulnerability data pipelines, both standard but demanding for four people.

defensibility.rationale: The core was Apache 2.0 open source and the scanner was positioned as a free alternative to Snyk and Dependabot, so copying was easy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: GitHub and Snyk already offered dependency scanning, and the project describes LunaTrace as a free alternative to them.

market_need_then: Data breach and compliance pressure motivated encryption tooling, and the 2021 Log4Shell incident drove demand for dependency scanning per a repo description. No spend evidence found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct and candid; the YC page says LunaSec is dead, fyi

rebrands.why: Product pivot; LunaTrace superseded the earlier tooling per the repository description

branding.community_and_virality: Open source repository on GitHub with sponsors page.

brand_strength.rationale: Some open source visibility on GitHub but no press on the brand found.

pivots.from: Open source data security and tokenization tooling
pivots.to: LunaTrace hosted open source dependency scanner
pivots.why: Not stated; a repository summary says LunaTrace was born from Log4Shell

outcome_analysis: LunaSec started as open source data protection tooling and pivoted to the LunaTrace dependency scanner, competing with free offerings from Snyk and GitHub Dependabot. The company is now dead per its own YC page note, but no post mortem gives a cause, so the failure factors are inferred from the product position and not confirmed.
